transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I’ve felt low and weighed down almost all the time for the last couple of years, and it just never really lifts. It is like this constant, heavy gray feeling that I just can't seem to shake off.
Have you had periods of feeling this low for most of the day, nearly every day, lasting for at least two years or more?

Yes, it has been pretty much every single day for a little over two years now, starting shortly after my spouse and I moved to the Bay Area. It has been completely continuous, without any real periods of relief where this heavy feeling actually lifted.
Can you recall any day or period during these last two years when your mood actually improved a bit in response to a positive event, even if just temporarily?

Not really, no. Even during moments that should be positive, like spending time with my spouse or doing hobbies I used to love like baking or stargazing, I can't remember feeling genuinely happy or light for more than a few fleeting minutes. It has just been a continuous, heavy gray feeling for the last two years without any real let-up.
Even when something good happens, like a compliment or a small success, do you ever notice even a brief shift in your mood, or does it stay completely flat or low?

It stays completely flat and low. Even when something positive happens, like getting a compliment or a small success at the lab, it doesn't lift that heavy, gray feeling in my chest. I honestly can't remember the last time I felt genuinely light or happy, even for just a few minutes.

Have you ever noticed even a short period of time — maybe a few hours or a day — during these last two years when your mood lifted noticeably, even if something small went well or you were with loved ones?

No, I really haven't noticed any stretch like that. At most, I might get distracted for a fleeting moment, but I can't recall feeling genuinely light or happy for more than a few minutes at a time. The heavy, gray feeling has been essentially continuous for the entire two years.
During the past two years, has your mood ever lightened up even briefly when something positive happened, such as being with close friends or experiencing a joyful event?

No, my mood almost never lightens up, even during those kinds of moments. Even when I am with my spouse or trying to do things I used to love, like baking or looking through my telescope, I can't remember the last time I felt genuinely happy or light for more than a few fleeting minutes. It just stays heavy.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic, low-grade depressed mood lasting for over two years with no significant periods of mood elevation or relief, even in response to positive events. The absence of major depressive episodes and the persistent nature of symptoms support a diagnosis of dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder).
